entry.title: A Resource Allocation Tournament
entry.summary:
We introduce and analyze a round-robin simultaneous resource allocation contest, motivated by sports leagues and other competitive environments where agents must distribute limited resources across multiple encounters. Players allocate resources in advance to matches against all opponents, and match outcomes are determined by relative allocations. We study two payoff schemes: total points, where players accumulate rewards for each win, and winner-takes-all, where only the tournament winner is rewarded.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #optimization #decision-theory

entry.title: A Weakly Group Strategy-Proof and Pareto-Stable Matching Mechanism with Two-Sided Indifferences under Gross Substitutes
entry.summary:
We study finite many-to-one matching markets with indifferences on both sides and publicly known firm preferences over sets of workers. A standard approach breaks ties uniformly at random and runs deferred acceptance, which is strategy-proof for workers but may select a weakly stable matching that is Pareto dominated under the agents' original preferences. For the broad class of markets in which each firm's preferences admit a gross substitutes (GS) representation, we construct a deterministic generalized deferred acceptance mechanism that is weakly stable, Pareto efficient with respect to both sides, worker weakly group strategy-proof, and implementable in strongly polynomial time given value oracles for the GS representations.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #market-design

entry.title: The Limits of Price Discrimination When the Market Is Unknown
entry.summary:
Bergemann, Brooks, and Morris (2015) characterize the consumer and producer surplus pairs that segmentation can produce when the distribution of values is known. I fix only the set of possible values and characterize the pairs that some market and some segmentation can produce. They form a convex polygon. Its outer edge is the largest efficient surplus a market can have when its uniform-price profit is capped, net of that profit, and truncated equal-revenue markets attain it.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #market-design #decision-theory

entry.title: Equilibria and Learning in Competitive Market Making. We propose a market-making game played among $N \ge 2$ strategic market makers and a single non-strategic representative trader.
entry.summary:
We propose a market-making game played among $N \ge 2$ strategic market makers and a single non-strategic representative trader. In a continuous quote space, standard finite-game arguments do not apply, while non-convex and discontinuous payoffs rule out classical continuous existence results and complicate learning. Nonetheless, we characterize pure-strategy Nash equilibria (PSNEs) and show that at least one PSNE always exists under minimal assumptions on the underlying asset value distribution, and that the equilibrium bid-ask spread widens strictly with asset value volatility.

Source: arXiv Quantitative Finance (q-fin.ST, q-fin.MF, q-fin.TR, q-fin.EC) · Tags: #quant-finance #market-design #decision-theory #ml-theory

entry.title: FairFRESH: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Fair and Explainable Household Food Recommendation
entry.summary:
Recommender systems typically serve one user at a time. However, in households, members share a finite pantry and follow different dietary rules, making independent recommendations prone to resource conflicts and dietary violations. We formulate household food recommendation as constrained fair division and present FairFRESH, a neuro-symbolic framework that learns per-member utilities, allocates foods under explicit welfare objectives, enforces dietary rules through a deterministic filter, and explains recommendations using Shapley and Banzhaf attributions.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #ml-theory #logic

entry.title: Network topology shapes consensus and vulnerability in LLM populations
entry.summary:
As large language models (LLMs) are deployed in interacting populations, their collective behaviour depends not only on the models but also on who interacts with whom. Studies of convention formation in LLM populations have mainly tested well-mixed interactions. We place policies extracted from four LLMs on fully connected, random regular, and heterogeneous networks, with $10^3$ to $10^5$ agents playing the naming game.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #ml-theory #consensus

entry.title: Balanced Posted Prices in Stationary Two-Sided Markets. We study an intermediary that buys nonperishing items from arriving sellers and sells them to arriving buyers, subject to limited storage.
entry.summary:
We study an intermediary that buys nonperishing items from arriving sellers and sells them to arriving buyers, subject to limited storage. Sellers and buyers arrive according to independent Poisson processes. The intermediary pays and charges the same fixed item prices, aiming to maximize long-run gains from trade: buyer value minus seller cost.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Spatial scaling of network length and shared-node density in bilayer distribution grids
entry.summary:
Certain distribution networks are built in layers, each layer collecting a commodity from the layer above it and delivering it to the layer below. We propose a minimal model that gives the length of each layer per unit area from the local density of demand, here the population density. Starting from the Beardwood, Halton and Hammersley law for minimal networks, the length of a layer depends on the number of nodes it reaches and on the area occupied by the users.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Matching Tasks to Agents: Mechanism Design for Multi-Agent Contracts. We study task assignment under adverse selection and moral hazard.
entry.summary:
We study task assignment under adverse selection and moral hazard. In the single-task setting, agents privately know their types, which determine their success probabilities and effort costs. Based on the agents' reported types, the principal selects an agent to perform the task and offers a success-contingent payment.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents

entry.title: A Personal History in Quantum Foundations: an Oral History Interview
entry.summary:
This oral history interview provides Yakir Aharonov's personal and conceptual recollections from the 1950s to the 2000s, focusing on his academic trajectory, some of his major contributions to quantum foundations, and his perspective on the development of the field. The interview traces Aharonov's academic career through the Technion, University of Bristol, Brandeis University, Yeshiva University, University of South Carolina, Tel Aviv University, George Mason University, and Chapman University. The interview also traces the development of Aharonov's work and collaborations on the EPR paradox, time-energy uncertainty relations, quantum measurement theory, quantum frames of reference, the two-state vector formalism, weak values, protective measurements, and several other contributions.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #quantum-computing

entry.title: Assortment optimization under the perception-adjusted Luce model. The Perception-Adjusted Luce Model (PALM) introduced by by Echenique et al.
entry.summary:
The Perception-Adjusted Luce Model (PALM) introduced by by Echenique et al. (2018) is a sequential choice model that can accommodate violations of regularity and choice overload, behaviors not captured by the utility-maximization framework. Flores et al. (2019) studied the assortment problem under the PALM and proved that, for the case of two levels, there is always an optimal solution that is revenue-ordered by level.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #optimization

entry.title: Strain Waves Generate Compression and Trigger Buckling in Active Polymers. Chemical reactions can sustain polymer motion without necessarily generating the compression required for buckling.
entry.summary:
Chemical reactions can sustain polymer motion without necessarily generating the compression required for buckling. Theory and simulations show that tension-dependent chemical transitions coupled to bond elasticity generate finite-wavelength traveling strain waves in a semiflexible polymer. In the straight chain at fixed axial span, the waves reduce mean active contraction while leaving mean elastic tension unchanged, generating compression that drives bending above a threshold.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Core-periphery structure induces double phase transitions in information cascades
entry.summary:
Double phase transitions in spreading processes are commonly associated with additional dynamical or structural complexity. Here, we show that such transitions can emerge naturally in prevalent networks exhibiting a core-periphery (CP) organization. Specifically, we consider threshold-driven spreading on CP networks constructed from the stochastic block model, which is characterized by three parameters: the relative core size $r$, the CP coupling strength $μ$, and the fraction of intra-block link allocation $α$.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems
